\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of an SDP optimizer]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.exists_sdp_optimizer}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.exists_sdp_optimizer}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsSDPAssignment, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpValue, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices
whose weights are nonnegative and symmetric, sum to $1$ over all ordered pairs of
vertices, and vanish on the diagonal. Then there is an assignment of unit vectors in
$\bbr^n$ to the vertices whose SDP value equals the supremum of the SDP values of all
such unit-vector assignments.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integral optimum bounded by the SDP optimum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum_le_sdpOptimum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum_le_sdpOptimum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on a finite vertex set of size $n$, with
nonnegative symmetric weights, total ordered-pair weight $1$, and zero diagonal weights.
Then the supremum of the cut values over all Boolean labelings is at most the supremum
of the SDP values over all assignments of unit vectors in $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gaussianRounding}
  {context}
  {vershynin-hdp-book}
  {pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b005,
    pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b006}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices,
and assign to each vertex $v$ a unit vector $U_v\in\mathbb R^n$. If $g$ has independent
standard Gaussian coordinates and each vertex is rounded according to the sign of
$\langle U_v,g\rangle$, then the expected cut value is
$\displaystyle\sum_{v,w}w(v,w)\,\frac{\arccos\langle U_v,U_w\rangle}{\pi}$, where the
cut value sums the weights of ordered pairs whose rounded labels differ.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of the Goemans–Williamson angle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle_spec}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle_spec}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle}
The Goemans–Williamson angle lies strictly between $0$ and $\pi$, satisfies
$\tan(\theta/2)=\theta$, and is the unique angle in that open interval satisfying
this equation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian Max-Cut constant identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant}
Let $\theta_*$ be the infimum of the angles $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ satisfying
$\tan(\theta/2)=\theta$, and let $c_*$ be the infimum of
$(\theta/\pi)/((1-\cos\theta)/2)$ over $0<\theta\leq\pi$. Then
$c_*=(\theta_*/\pi)/((1-\cos\theta_*)/2)$.
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant}
  {direct}
  {mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}
  {pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b007}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices with
nonnegative symmetric weights summing to $1$ and zero diagonal, and let $U$ assign a
unit vector in $\bbr^n$ to each vertex. The Goemans–Williamson constant times the SDP
value of $U$ is at most the expected cut value obtained by Gaussian rounding, where the
expectation is over $n$ independent standard Gaussian coordinates.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices with
nonnegative symmetric weights summing to $1$ and zero diagonal, and let $U$ assign a
unit vector in $\bbr^n$ to each vertex whose SDP value equals the SDP optimum. Suppose
$	heta$ lies between the Goemans–Williamson angle and $\pi$, inclusive, and
$(1-\cos\theta)/2$ is at most the SDP optimum. Then the expected cut value from
Gaussian rounding of $U$, with respect to $n$ independent standard Gaussian coordinates,
is at least $\theta/\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimal values for the five-cycle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle_optima}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle_optima}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsSDPAssignment, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycleSDP, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpValue}
For the weighted five-cycle on vertices indexed by $\bbr/5\bbr$, with weight $1/10$ on
each ordered adjacent pair and zero weight otherwise, the weights are nonnegative and
symmetric, sum to $1$, and vanish on the diagonal; its maximum cut value is $4/5$. The
assignment placing vertex $v$ at the unit vector with first two coordinates
$(\cos(4\pi v/5),\sin(4\pi v/5))$ and all other coordinates zero has SDP value
$(1-\cos(4\pi/5))/2$, and this value is the SDP optimum.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Almost-sure rounded cut value for the five-cycle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle_rounding_optimal}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle_rounding_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycleSDP, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gaussianRounding, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
Let $g=(g_0,\ldots,g_4)$ be sampled from the product of five standard Gaussian
probability measures on $\mathbb R$. With probability one, rounding the five-cycle SDP
vectors by the signs of their inner products with $g$ produces a cut of value $4/5$.
\end{theorem}
